lead: Labour is regular painful contractions that cause progressive effacement and dilatation of the cervix, ending in the birth of the baby and placenta. Normal labour: spontaneous onset at term (37–42 wk), single cephalic vertex, vaginal birth, 3–18 h, no complications.
f: Diagnose by painful regular contractions + a changing cervix; show and bulging forewaters support it · True labour: regular, closer, stronger; abdomen to back; cervix dilates; not relieved by sedation · False (Braxton Hicks): irregular, unchanged, lower abdomen, no cervical change, relieved by rest

sc: 39 wk, irregular tightenings relieved by rest, cervix closed → False labour: send home

f: First stage: onset to full dilatation · latent 0–4 cm; active from 4 cm (open the partogram) · primi 12–18 h, multi 6–8 h; about 1 cm/h or more in the active phase · Second stage: full dilatation to birth: primi up to 2 h (3 h with epidural), multi 1 h (2 h with epidural) · Third stage: birth to placenta, 5–15 min; retained if over 30 min with active management · Fourth stage: recovery; highest PPH risk: observe at least 4 h

sc: Cervix 5 cm, 3 contractions in 10 min → Active phase: start the partogram

f: Power: 3–5 contractions in 10 min, 40–60 s, fundal dominance · More than 5 in 10 min: fetal hypoxia, uterine rupture · Upper segment contracts and retracts; thin lower segment stretches (physiological retraction ring) · Passenger: vertex, OA, well flexed; posterior fontanelle (Y, 3 sutures) gives the position · Passage: gynaecoid 50%, android 20% (OP, deep transverse arrest), anthropoid 25% (face to pubis), platypelloid 5% (inlet delay)

sc: Six contractions in 10 min on oxytocin → Stop oxytocin: hypoxia and rupture risk

f: Inlet: AP 11 cm (true conjugate), transverse 13 cm: head enters transverse · Mid-cavity round 12 cm (spines 10.5): head rotates · Outlet: AP 13, transverse 11 cm: head leaves AP · Diagonal conjugate 12.5 cm (promontory not reached = adequate inlet) · Engaged: biparietal (9.5 cm) past the inlet = 2/5 or less palpable · Station: lowest bony point vs the spines (−5 to +5) · High head at term in a primi: think CPD, praevia, wrong dates

Engagement · Descent · Flexion (SOB 9.5 cm presents) · Internal rotation (occiput 1/8 forward at the pelvic floor) · Extension (born under the symphysis) · Restitution · External rotation (shoulders AP) · Expulsion (anterior shoulder first) · Deflexed OP: occipito-frontal 11.5 cm; brow: mento-vertical 13.5 cm (largest) · Caput crosses sutures, gone in days; cephalhaematoma stops at sutures and grows on day 2 · Severe moulding + caput = obstruction

sc: Scalp swelling limited by suture lines, growing on day 2 → Cephalhaematoma

f: Admission: history, vitals, abdomen (fifths, contractions, FHR), VE · Partogram from 4 cm; VE every 4 h (2 h on oxytocin); contractions every 30 min · Low risk: intermittent auscultation every 15–30 min for 1 min after a contraction; high risk: continuous CTG · Pulse 30 min, BP 4-hourly, temperature 2-hourly, urine · Companion, mobile, fluids, empty bladder · Pain relief ladder to epidural; pethidine not near birth

tr: No routine ARM, enema, shaving or oxytocin in normal labour

f: Full dilatation on VE; urge to push, head visible · FHR every 5 min (low risk) · Push with contractions · Control the head at crowning, support the perineum · Feel for cord round the neck; clamp and cut if tight · Gentle downward traction for the anterior shoulder, then upward · Episiotomy not routine: mediolateral for instruments, fetal distress, shoulder dystocia, breech, tight perineum

sc: Multi, fully dilated 1 h, no epidural → Delay: assess for instrumental birth

f: Separation through the spongy decidua; crossed fibres act as living ligatures · Schultze (80%, fetal surface first) or Matthews Duncan (20%, edge first, more bleeding) · Signs: fundus rises and firms, cord lengthens, gush of blood · Active management (AMTSL): oxytocin 10 IU IM within 1 min (misoprostol 600 µg oral if none) + controlled cord traction with counter-pressure; then check uterine tone (WHO) · Ergometrine 0.5 mg only if BP normal · Delayed cord clamping 1–3 min · Retained placenta: 30 min active (60 min physiological) → manual removal · Check the placenta, cord vessels (2 arteries + 1 vein), tears

tr: Never pull the cord without a contraction and counter-pressure: cord snap or uterine inversion
Exclude a second twin before any uterotonic
sc: Shock with no fundus felt after strong cord pulling → Acute uterine inversion: replace at once

f: At least 4 h on the labour ward: pulse, BP, fundus and bleeding every 30 min; bladder; early breastfeeding · Apgar at 1 and 5 min: appearance, pulse, grimace, activity, respiration; 7–10 normal, 4–6 support, 0–3 resuscitate
